note: The job creation page has two admission paths. Without JavaScript the templ form posts to /create, where every field arrives as a string and an empty one is resolved against the defaults before the configuration is built. With the bundle loaded CreateJobIsland posts POST /api/v1/jobs, where the raw body decides which keys the caller wrote and a value the defaults would replace is refused outright (docs/behavior-invariants.md, 'A written field is used as written'). This file is the contract that keeps the two producing one stored configuration. Each case names a form submission exactly as the browser would send it -- an unchecked checkbox is an absent key, an emptied number is an empty string -- and the JSON body the island must build from it. web/src/createJobBody.test.ts checks buildCreateJobBody against every case, and internal/server/create_job_parity_test.go submits both halves to the real handlers and compares the stored JobConfig. Neither implementation is the source of truth; this file is.

cases.name: form defaults
cases.note: Every control at the value the templ fallback ships, nothing touched. It covers both halves of the hazard at once: batchSize is rendered as 0 meaning 'decide for me', so the island has to omit it or the API would refuse a request the form accepts, while seed is rendered as 0 meaning 'draw one', which ApplyDefaults leaves alone and so travels as an explicit zero. The four early-stopping fields are blank and disabled, and the CMA-ES section is submitted by the fallback whatever engine is selected, so a MayFly job has to drop it exactly as parseCMAESForm does. optimizerRestarts is rendered as 1, which ApplyDefaults leaves alone, so it travels as written rather than being omitted the way a defaulted zero is.

cases.name: batch run with polishing and early stopping
cases.note: A fully specified batch job. Convergence detection is switched off, which the form can only express by omitting the checkbox, so the body has to carry disableConvergence beside a false convergenceEnabled -- sending the false alone would be defaulted straight back to true. stopMinIters is an explicit zero the API accepts as written, because ApplyDefaults never fills the early-stopping fields. optimizerRestarts is above its default here, which is what multiplies the projected cost.

cases.name: cmaes with an emptied initial sigma
cases.note: The CMA-ES section travels only for a CMA-ES job. An emptied step size is the interesting one: the form handler substitutes the CMA-ES default before it builds the configuration, and the island omits the key so ApplyDefaults substitutes the same number. An unchecked active-adaptation box is the only way either path can express a disabled negative rank-mu update, so the body sends false rather than omitting it. It also carries the one CMA-ES combination of restarts and restart strategy app accepts: sixteen independent cold attempts with the none strategy, which is what an evaluation-matched restart arm asks for. IPOP or BIPOP beside a restart count other than one is refused, so it cannot appear here.

cases.name: dragonfly with a canvas path
cases.note: A second engine that reads none of the CMA-ES section, so the island has to drop all four fields there too rather than special-casing CMA-ES's absence; app.Validate refuses a CMA-ES-only field on a Dragonfly job instead of ignoring it. The canvas path is filled in here, and an emptied optimizer epochs field, and an emptied restart count beside it, stand for the omit-the-blank rule on controls the fallback ships with a value.

cases.name: budget-filling restart cap
cases.note: A negative restart count, which is the budget-filling shape rather than a fixed number of attempts: the stage is capped at abs(N) times its iteration budget and keeps launching cold attempts until no further whole one fits. It travels as written on both paths, because the sign is the request. The island cannot reuse the omit-a-zero rule to normalize it and the form handler bounds the magnitude rather than the value, so -8 has to survive as -8 instead of arriving as 8 or as the default 1. A MayFly job, because internal/app/cmaes.go refuses any count but 1 beside an IPOP or BIPOP ladder, negatives included.
